updates.title: MongoDB beyond JSON: agents, memory and models
updates.text: We tested MongoDB for agents and memory with real Voyage embeddings. Both databases found the same nearest results; tools can repeat after a crash and cached answers can outlive a policy change.

updates.title: Routing by our own rulebook, measured again: three fresh runs of the routed arm
updates.text: Pre-registered verdict: routing beats always-Opus, within a wide replicate allowance, and does not beat always-Luna.

updates.title: Does routing by our own rulebook beat one fixed model on real tasks?
updates.text: Eight real coding tasks, three arms, three runs each, scored by the share of hidden test cases fixed (no task was fully solved). Per case fixed, a table copied from our routing rule paid 13.3 cents (61% of cases), always Opus 5.5 paid 24.7 (65%) and always GPT-6 Luna paid 4.3 (52%). The pre-registered verdict is incomplete: one routed cell hit its spend stop.

updates.title: What does a defect caught in review cost, model by model?
updates.text: Four models on one tool-free review seat caught between 26 and 31 of 60 defects, all within noise, at 0.06 to 8.3 cents a review. gpt-oss-120b, MiniMax M3.1 Flash and Claude Opus 5.5 are on the pre-registered frontier; Claude Sonnet 5.5 is not.

updates.title: Does the same model cost the same through every broker?
updates.text: Measured on 720 identical calls: two brokers billed exactly list price for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-4o mini, the third 10% above it on both, a spread of 1.10 against a pre-registered bar of 1.05. No broker served a different model.

updates.title: Can a reviewer talk itself out of its false alarms?
updates.text: No. Asked to name a concrete failing input for every finding or drop it, MiniMax M3.1 Flash kept 249 of 269 of its own findings. False alarms stayed at 20 and 22 of 30 clean changes, against a pre-registered bar of 2.

updates.title: A free model on our review bench
updates.text: On a sealed corpus of 30 real defects and 30 clean changes, MiniMax M3.1 Flash's counts sat in Claude Opus's range at about 1.5 cents a review. No reviewer flags few enough clean changes to vote, and an agent-run reviewer can read its own answer key.

updates.title: Can a free model find real bugs in our private code?
updates.text: On bugs in our private fix history that can be found from the code alone, MiniMax M3.1 Flash's first guess landed within two lines of the fix 63% of the time, against 23% for our current default. Only about 1 in 10 of the small fixes we sampled could be found that way.

updates.title: Where would MongoDB earn a place in Odin?
updates.text: 99,000 requests and a separate 19,800-request repeat found two advantages over monolithic JSONB, but none over the stronger PostgreSQL alternatives, for these workloads on one machine. All seventeen outcomes and the durability amendment are retained.

updates.title: Does flexible workflow data need MongoDB?
updates.text: Both stores passed 20,000 operations, 42 correctness checks and ten evolution suites behind Temporal activities. For this workload, a MongoDB advantage remains unresolved and flexible JSON alone gave no demonstrated reason to switch.
